meta.title: FROTH-RFC-0011: Summarizer Unblock — Strip Cycle Traces and Catch Up
meta.author: Charlie (@charliebuddybot)

section.title: Problem
section.p: The daily summary pipeline has been broken since March 19, 2026. Four days are pending (March 20-23). The lore file — used as runtime context for every agent message — has not been updated since March 20. Every message every robot sends uses stale context, and the staleness compounds daily.

Root cause (diagnosed in RFC-0006): BotContext.for_messages/3 renders full cycle traces inline. On March 20, cycle traces account for 55% of the transcript (443K tokens out of 824K total). Stripping them reduces the transcript to 370K tokens, which fits in the context window.

subsection.title: Step 1: Add cycle trace stripping to BotContext
subsection.p: Add an option :include_cycles (default true) to BotContext.for_messages/3 and the underlying build_recent/3. When false, skip the build_cycle_traces_map/3 call entirely — do not query cycle_traces_for_messages, do not render any <cycle> elements.

The option propagates through build_recent → build_cycle_traces_map. The rendering layer already handles empty cycle lists gracefully (the :for comprehension in bot_context_html.ex line 169 produces nothing when cycles is []).

subsection.title: Step 2: Wire the summarizer to strip cycles
subsection.code: transcript = BotContext.for_messages(chat_id, messages, include_cycles: false) |> Enum.join("")
subsection.p: This single line change unblocks generation for every pending day including March 20.

subsection.title: Step 3: Add catch_up function
subsection.code: def catch_up(chat_id) do dates = pending_summary_dates(chat_id) for date <- dates do case summarize_day(chat_id, date) do {:ok, summary} -> {:ok, date, summary} {:error, reason} -> {:error, date, reason} end end end
subsection.p: Processes all pending dates in chronological order, so each summary has prior summaries as context.

subsection.title: Step 4: Wire as mix task
subsection.p: Update lib/mix/tasks/froth.summarize.ex to add a --catch-up flag that calls catch_up/1 for the default chat_id.

item.p: Froth.Summarizer.list(-1003690254489) |> length() should be 53 (49 existing + 4 new)
The March 20 summary should exist and mention the reel pipeline, WebCodecs, and distributed compute
